text: For vectors a and b in R^3, the magnitude |a x b| equals:
choices: |a||b| cos(theta), the scalar projection of a onto b
|a||b| sin(theta), the area of the parallelogram they span
explanation: The cross-product magnitude |a x b| = |a||b| sin(theta) equals the area of the parallelogram spanned by a and b, and the vector itself is perpendicular to both. The expression |a||b| cos(theta) is the dot product, a scalar, not the cross-product magnitude.
